headline: Indian Markets Surge as Sensex Gains Over 2,000 Points Amid Falling Oil Prices and Strong Global Cues

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Sharp decline in global crude oil prices easing inflationary pressure
Significant surge in foreign capital inflows into Indian equities
Positive global market cues and reactions to US political developments
Strong quarterly earnings reports from major domestic companies
whatHappening: Sensex jumped 2,009 points to close above the 24,500 mark, marking a seven-month high
Bharti Airtel reported a 24% increase in net profit to ₹10,710 crore for the September quarter
The Mines Ministry launched the ninth round of auctions for 20 critical mineral blocks
Noel Tata is set to retire as vice-chairman of Titan Company on November 12
summary: Indian benchmark indices witnessed their biggest gains in seven months, with the Sensex skyrocketing over 2,000 points driven by falling crude prices and foreign flows. Bharti Airtel led corporate news with a 24% profit jump, while the government initiated new critical mineral auctions. Investor wealth increased by approximately Rs 7 lakh crore as Nifty and Sensex rallied nearly 2%.
